result_text:
I changed the mock-folder rule so any folder whose name starts with `mock` or `__mock` counts as test code, and added a regression test. The full `codeanalyzer` suite passes (107 test classes, no failures).

**What changed**
- `codeanalyzer/src/main/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventions.java` (lines 393–394): the two mock regexes now end in `[^/]*` instead of `[a-zA-Z0-9_\- ]+`. That lets the suffix be empty (plain `mock/`) and carry any punctuation or non-ASCII characters, while the match still stops at the folder boundary. Backslash paths are covered by the existing normalisation in `SourceFileFilter.pathMatches`.
- New `codeanalyzer/src/test/java/nl/obren/sokrates/sourcecode/scoping/ScopingConventionsTest.java` (JUnit 4, matching most of the module). It covers:
  - the new cases: `mock/`, `mock.data/`, `mock(old)/`, `mock-größe/`, `mock模拟/`, `__mock/`, and Windows-style paths;
  - the previously matched folders (`mocks/`, `__mocks__/`, `mock-data/`, `mock_data/`, `mock data/`, `mockStore/`);
  - the negatives (`remock/`, `demo/`, `src/main/java/`, `mock.java`, `mockery.java`).

**Notes**
- The regex keeps the existing `.*/` prefix, so a mock folder at the very root of a relative path (e.g. `mock/x.java` with no leading slash) still depends on how paths are stored. The other rules share this behaviour; I did not change it.
- Nothing is committed.
